photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Vizcaya Museum and Gardens Miami Biscayne Bay villa facade
photo.prompt: Golden-hour photo of Vizcaya Museum and Gardens from Biscayne Bay, with the villa, stone barge, palms and water in frame

slides.headline: Vizcaya’s villa cost $15M by 1922
slides.body: The villa was built mainly from 1914 to 1922, while the gardens and village outbuildings continued into 1923.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Vizcaya Museum and Gardens aerial Italian Renaissance gardens Miami
photo.prompt: Overhead photo of Vizcaya’s formal gardens, villa, coral stone paths and Biscayne Bay shoreline

slides.headline: That started with James Deering in 1910
slides.body: Deering bought land in Coconut Grove for Vizcaya after leaving daily work at International Harvester in 1909.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons James Deering portrait Vizcaya
photo.prompt: Historic portrait of James Deering with a dark museum background and a faint Biscayne Bay estate outline behind him

slides.headline: And the site covered 180 acres on Biscayne Bay
slides.body: The property included shoreline mangrove wetlands and dense native tropical forest.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Vizcaya Museum and Gardens Biscayne Bay mangroves Coconut Grove
photo.prompt: Wide photo of Vizcaya’s Biscayne Bay shoreline with mangroves, tropical trees and the villa visible beyond the water

slides.headline: Which led to construction in 1912
slides.body: F. Burrall Hoffman was the architect, Paul Chalfin directed the design, and Diego Suarez designed the landscape.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Vizcaya Museum and Gardens construction historic Miami 1910s
photo.prompt: Black-and-white style scene of early 1910s construction at Vizcaya, with workers, stone blocks, scaffolding and Biscayne Bay nearby

slides.headline: Then Deering arrived by yacht on Christmas 1916
slides.body: Deering began occupying Vizcaya on Christmas Day 1916 after arriving aboard his yacht Nepenthe.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Vizcaya stone barge Biscayne Bay Miami
photo.prompt: Low-angle photo of Vizcaya’s stone barge on Biscayne Bay with the villa behind it and dark water in the foreground

slides.headline: So the private estate is public today
slides.body: Miami-Dade County owns Vizcaya Museum and Gardens, and the property is open to the public in Coconut Grove.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Vizcaya Museum and Gardens entrance Miami visitors
photo.prompt: Present-day photo of the Vizcaya Museum and Gardens entrance, with the villa, gardens and palms framed as a public landmark

Vizcaya started as James Deering’s 180-acre Biscayne Bay estate and became a public Miami-Dade museum.
